## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
tcga_rna_count_data_crc <- read_csv("~/Documents/Master Bioinformatics & Systems biology/Scientific Machine Learning/TCGA_dataset 2/tcga_rna_count_data_crc.csv")

prediction_file_crc <- read_csv("~/Documents/Master Bioinformatics & Systems biology/Scientific Machine Learning/TCGA_dataset 2/prediction_file_crc.csv")
```

```{r}
str(prediction_file_crc)

summary(prediction_file_crc)
```

```{r}
prediction_file_crc$TP53 <- factor(prediction_file_crc$TP53, levels = c("WT", "SNV"))
prediction_file_crc$KRAS <- factor(prediction_file_crc$KRAS, levels = c("WT", "SNV"))
prediction_file_crc$BRAF <- factor(prediction_file_crc$BRAF, levels = c("WT", "SNV"))
prediction_file_crc$APC  <- factor(prediction_file_crc$APC,  levels = c("WT", "SNV"))
prediction_file_crc$TTN  <- factor(prediction_file_crc$TTN,  levels = c("WT", "SNV"))
 
table(prediction_file_crc$TP53)
table(prediction_file_crc$KRAS)
table(prediction_file_crc$BRAF)
table(prediction_file_crc$APC)
table(prediction_file_crc$TTN)
```

```{r}
colSums(is.na(prediction_file_crc))

# Simple WT vs SNV association tests (Wilcoxon) + BH-FDR
# assumes prediction_file_crc is already loaded

df <- prediction_file_crc

genes  <- c("TP53","KRAS","BRAF","APC","TTN")
traits <- c("TMB","TBL","fraction_genome_altered","aneuploidy_score")

# make mutation columns factors (WT reference)
for (g in genes) df[[g]] <- factor(df[[g]], levels = c("WT","SNV"))

# run all tests
out <- data.frame()
for (g in genes) {
  for (t in traits) {
    p <- wilcox.test(df[[t]] ~ df[[g]], exact = FALSE)$p.value
    out <- rbind(out, data.frame(gene=g, trait=t, p_value=p))
  }
}

# multiple testing correction (20 tests)
out$p_adj_BH <- p.adjust(out$p_value, method = "BH")

# show results sorted by adjusted p-value
out <- out[order(out$p_adj_BH), ]
print(out)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

df <- prediction_file_crc

# Ensure TP53 is factor
df$TP53 <- factor(df$TP53, levels = c("WT","SNV"))

# 1️⃣ TMB (log scale)
ggplot(df, aes(x = TP53, y = TMB)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "TP53 Mutation vs TMB",
       y = "TMB (log scale)")

# 2️⃣ TBL (log scale)
ggplot(df, aes(x = TP53, y = TBL + 1)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "TP53 Mutation vs TBL",
       y = "TBL (log scale)")

# 3️⃣ Fraction Genome Altered
ggplot(df, aes(x = TP53, y = fraction_genome_altered)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "TP53 Mutation vs Fraction Genome Altered",
       y = "Fraction Genome Altered")

# 4️⃣ Aneuploidy Score
ggplot(df, aes(x = TP53, y = aneuploidy_score)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "TP53 Mutation vs Aneuploidy Score",
       y = "Aneuploidy Score")
```
